name: Isoniazid
summary: Cornerstone bactericidal anti-TB drug for active and latent tuberculosis; inhibits mycolic acid synthesis.
mechanism: Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis (via InhA), disrupting the mycobacterial cell wall — bactericidal against actively dividing tubercle bacilli.
targets: InhA (enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase) in mycolic acid synthesis
pharmacodynamics: Concentration-dependent killing with a post-antibiotic effect against M. tuberculosis.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic — NAT2 acetylation (also a CYP2E1 inhibitor)

dosing.adult: 5 mg/kg (max 300 mg) PO once daily; latent TB: 300 mg daily (or 900 mg twice-weekly under DOT)

safety.pregnancy: Use when TB treatment is indicated (standard of care, with pyridoxine)
safety.lactation: Compatible — small amounts in milk; give pyridoxine to the infant
warnings: Hepatotoxicity — risk increased by age > 35, alcohol, and rifampin co-administration
Peripheral neuropathy — prevent with pyridoxine (vitamin B6)

clinicalPearls: Always co-administer pyridoxine (25-50 mg/day) to prevent neuropathy
Hepatotoxicity is the main serious toxicity — alcohol and age > 35 raise the risk
good: Cornerstone bactericidal drug for active and latent TB.
bad: Hepatotoxicity, neuropathy without B6, and significant drug interactions.
